nodes.title: About Prompt Gen Adjustments
widgets_values:
These allow you to specify adjustments to the generated prompt.

User Clarifications allows you to specify characteristics of the image the prompt generator might otherwise struggle with interpreting. Such as "Her legs are crossed, with her hand resting on her knee" 

Ending Tags allows you to include certain captions at the end of the prompt.

nodes.title: System Prompt
widgets_values:
# Prompting Formula

Build one paragraph filling in these categories:

A (photography type) of a (beautiful) (ethnicity) (subject) adult woman with (facial features), (body characteristics), and (hair). She (gazes) with (expression) and (mouth expression) as she (action) in a (pose), her (arm/hand/leg/foot positioning). (outfit). The scene takes place in (environment) with (background) and (props). The image is illuminated by (lighting type) with (lighting direction) and (lighting quality). (shot type) with (subject placement), photographed from (camera angle) with a (camera perspective). Captured on a (lens focal length) (camera type) using (depth of field), (focus behavior), (exposure), and (camera behavior). Rendered with (realism), (texture), and (color grading).

Comma-join the clauses into a single sentence ending with a period. Do not invent props, wardrobe, or colors the scene does not support — over-specifying dilutes control.

# Forbidden Output: Do not describe the image as anything other than a realistic medium; no illustration, painting, anime, manga, CGI, digital art, concept art, cartoon, cel-shaded work, render, or similar.

nodes.title: Model Links
widgets_values:
## Model Links 


**diffusion_models**

- [Krea 2 Models](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/tree/main/diffusion_models)  

**text_encoders**
- [bf16 text encoder](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen3-VL/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors) better than fp8 but larger
- [fp8 text encoder](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen3-VL/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) 

- [Abliterated text encoder](https://huggingface.co/ahmed22xa/Huihui-Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-abliterated-comfy/tree/main) can be used instead if you want to do NSFW prompt gens (normal text encoders are censored) 

**vae**

- [qwen_image_vae.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/resolve/main/vae/qwen_image_vae.safetensors)

**loras**

- [TextFusion Refusal](https://civitai.com/models/2775340/krea2-textfusion-refusal-reduction-lora?modelVersionId=3125118)
- [Turbo LoRA](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/blob/main/loras/krea2_turbo_lora_rank_64_bf16.safetensors) this is only needed if you use the Raw model.

**custom nodes**

- [Krea2T-Enhancer](https://github.com/capitan01R/ComfyUI-Krea2T-Enhancer)

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/

│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/

│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   └── qwen_image_vae.safetensors
│   └── 📂 loras/
│       └── LoRA files
```

nodes.title: About Style Adjustment Tags
widgets_values:
You may not want to use all of these at once, or at a full -1.0 strength, as certain creative concepts are associated with them.

Toy around with them to find a balance you like between realism and stylization.

nodes.title: Note about Models
widgets_values:
This workflow is by-default set up using the full Krea 2 Raw model with the Turbo LoRA at 0.6 strength, which provides good quality at reasonable speeds.

However, you can use any of the Krea 2 models with this workflow. Just swap out the models and adjust the samplers to your liking.

nodes.title: Note about Samplers
widgets_values:
I've provided two k-sampler setups you can use in this workflow. A basic one. And a 2-pass advanced one to get the best quality.

By default I've disabled the 2-pass k-sampler. To enable it, select the nodes and Ctrl+B

nodes.title: Note about Noise Amount
widgets_values:
This affects the balance between the source image and generated image. The higher the value, the more the samplers override the input image.

In my experience:
- 0.4 works well for detail refinement on semi-realistic images.
- 0.5 sometimes has an uncanny blend between stylized and realistic.
- 0.55 - 0.6 achieves good realism while retaining the composition of the source image.
- 0.65 begins to drift towards the composition of the generated image.
- 0.7 - 0.75 varies in quality depending on the generation; how good it looks largely depends on how good the full sampler image itself looks.
- 0.8+ typically drifts too far from the source image.
___________

What I like to do is start on 0.6, and then experiment with 0.7 for more realism, and 0.4-5 for more style.

nodes.title: Note about Negative Prompting
widgets_values:
Negative prompts become ineffective at 1 CFG, which is what Turbo models/loras are built around.

However, if using the Raw Krea 2 model with the Turbo LoRA at 0.6 strength, higher CFG can still be used.

Increasing CFG to 2 seems to work well if you want negative prompting. But generations will take twice as long.

However, CFG above 1 might conflict with the prompt weights node.

nodes.title: System Prompt Addition
widgets_values:
## User Clarifications

Treat the following statements as factual descriptions of the reference image. If any statement differs from your visual interpretation, prioritize these statements. Incorporate them naturally into the generated prompt.

nodes.title: Default System Prompt
widgets_values:
# Prompting Formula

Build one paragraph filling in these categories:

A (shot type), (photography type) of (beauty) (ethnicity) (subject) adult woman with (facial features), (body characteristics), and (hair). She (gazes) with (expression) and (mouth expression) as she (action) in a (pose), her (arm/hand/leg/foot positioning). (outfit). The scene takes place in (environment) with (background) and (props). The image is illuminated by (lighting type) with (lighting direction) and (lighting quality). (composition) with (subject placement), photographed from (camera angle) with a (camera perspective). Captured on a (lens focal length) (camera type) using (depth of field), (focus behavior), (exposure), and (camera behavior). Rendered with (realism), (film stock/style), (texture), and (color grading).

Comma-join the clauses into a single sentence ending with a period. Do not invent props, wardrobe, or colors the scene does not support — over-specifying dilutes control.

nodes.title: Note about Prompt Generation
widgets_values:
Realism conversions are very reliant on specific prompting, as you're aiming to recreate a realistic version of the reference image to blend with it.

However, doing so with Krea 2 isn't easy due to its cinematographic language. Luckily it also comes with a language model we can use to help with that, and since Krea 2 was trained with AI generated captions, the outputs tend to overlap with its understanding.

However... this also requires generating a good system prompt for it to use. I've played around with these a bit, and I've included one that I found works reasonably well.

_____

For ideal results you may want to make further manual adjustments to the generated prompt.

nodes.title: About Krea2 Prompt Weights
widgets_values:
This node is new at the time of me posting this workflow, so you may need to update your kjnodes to "nightly"
_____

This node enables you to use prompt weights with Krea 2, such as (tag:2), to increase or decrease their effect.

This is important for realism transfers, as we are able to use weights like (anime:-1.0) to disable certain stylized outputs.

nodes.title: About Krea2T Enhancer Node
widgets_values:
The Krea2T-Enhancer helps with prompt understanding. It's not required, but I've found it improves results.

The node is new, so you may need to download it from the [Github page](https://github.com/capitan01R/ComfyUI-Krea2T-Enhancer)
